newsitem.title: INDIA: India to hold trials for pepper exchange in June.
newsitem.headline: India to hold trials for pepper exchange in June.

text.p: India will hold trial runs in June ahead of the start of the country's first international futures exchange for pepper, a government statement said on Monday.
"Mock trading is being organised later this month. The commercial banks are being invited to the mock trading so that they can have experience of trading and clearing," the statement said.
Procedural snags had delayed India's ambitious plans to start the exchange by the end of April.
The statement did not set a new date for the start of the exchange.
In February, the Food Ministry announced that the country's first international exchange and clearing house for pepper would start functioning at the southern Indian city of Cochin by April.
India's cabinet decided in the second half of 1995 to upgrade the domestic futures commodity exchange, run by the Indian Pepper and Spices Trade Association (IPSTA), into an international exchange.
The domestic exchange has 140 members and the annual volume of trade is about six billion rupees ($168 million).
The statement said the progress made on the start of the exchange was reviewed at a meeting of officials in New Delhi on Monday.
It said five million rupees had been collected from members enrolled for trading at the international exchange towards equity capital of the First Commodity Clearing Corporation of India (FCCI).
Commercial banks were seeking permission from the Reserve Bank of India to contribute to the equity capital of the clearing corporation, it said.

The statement said the Jakarta-based International Pepper Community would organise a workshop at Cochin for potential participants, banks and other institutions. ($1 = 35.8 rupees) --New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
